ap_biology-m01.set_intro: A student counted the cells in each stage of the cell cycle in a sample of 500 cells from the growing tip of an onion root. The cell cycle of these cells takes 24 hours. The table shows the number of cells in each stage.

stimulus.description: Number of cells in each stage in a sample of cells from an onion root tip

items.stem: Which statement best describes the data in the table?

options.text: Most of the cells are in mitosis, because a growing root tip divides all of the time.
options.why: Fewer than half of the cells are in a stage of mitosis.

options.text: Most of the cells are in interphase, and the number of cells decreases from prophase to metaphase to anaphase.
options.why: 390 of the 500 cells are in interphase, and the numbers are 50, 25 and 15 in prophase, metaphase and anaphase.

options.text: Most of the cells are in telophase, because the cells are about to divide.
options.why: Only a small number of cells are in telophase.

options.text: The cells are spread equally among all of the stages of the cell cycle.
options.why: The numbers in the table are very different from one another.

blueprint.subject: ap_biology
blueprint.concept: describe the distribution of cells among the stages of the cell cycle in a table
student_thinking: Identify the biological principle or relationship that governs the situation: describe the distribution of cells among the stages of the cell cycle in a table
Apply it to the information given and compare the result with the four options

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

must_include: the number of cells in each stage

misconceptions.description: Fewer than half of the cells are in a stage of mitosis.
Only a small number of cells are in telophase.
The numbers in the table are very different from one another.

verification.independent_path: sum of the stage counts vs the sample size and the ordering of the counts

blueprint.judgment_demand: choose the governing biological relationship, then apply or interpret it

items.stem: The mitotic index is the percent of the cells in the sample that are in a stage of mitosis (prophase, metaphase, anaphase or telophase). What is the mitotic index of the sample?

options.why: The cells in mitosis are 50+25+15+20=110 of 500, which is 22.0%.
Divides the number of cells in mitosis by the number of cells in interphase.
Gives the number of cells in mitosis instead of the percent of the cells.
Divides the number of cells in prophase by the sample size.

items.stem: Assume that the time that a cell spends in a stage is proportional to the fraction of the cells that are in that stage. About how long does a cell spend in prophase?

options.text: 2.40 hours
options.why: The fraction in prophase is 50/500, so the time is 24 h x 0.100 = 2.40 hours.

options.text: 10.00 hours
options.why: Uses the percent of cells in prophase as the number of hours.

options.text: 1,200 hours
options.why: Multiplies the cell cycle time by the number of cells in prophase instead of the fraction.

options.text: 3.60 hours
options.why: Includes the cells in metaphase with the cells in prophase.

items.stem: The student treats the root tip with a drug that prevents the formation of the spindle fibers and counts the cells again after several hours. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: The percent of cells in metaphase would increase, because the chromosomes could not be pulled apart and the cells would stay in metaphase.
options.why: Without spindle fibers the sister chromatids are not separated, so cells accumulate before anaphase.

options.text: The percent of cells in interphase would decrease to zero, because all of the cells would enter mitosis.
options.why: Cells would not all enter mitosis, and the cells that are blocked would stay in metaphase.

options.text: The percent of cells in anaphase would increase, because the chromosomes would be pulled apart more quickly.
options.why: A drug that blocks the spindle fibers prevents the chromosomes from being pulled apart.

options.text: The percent of cells in telophase would increase, because the nuclei would form without separating the chromosomes.
options.why: Telophase follows anaphase, and cells that cannot separate their chromosomes do not reach it.
